A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same matrix-factorization framework and MAFALDA-SGD algorithm. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching renumbered and relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original privacy-accounting comparisons across communication graphs and Housing regression experiments, including repeated-run learning curves and privacy–utility results in Section 7 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original privacy-accounting and Housing experiments and adds FEMNIST classification results and a Housing comparison on Misskey.

M1.justification: Remark 3 and Appendix A.7 extend the fixed-gossip MF-D-SGD formulation to round-dependent matrices W_t, adapting workload construction and averaging. The core MAFALDA-SGD objective and local correlation structure remain unchanged. Algorithm 2's added optimization line documents a step already described in v1.

E1.justification: v2 substantially broadens evaluation beyond Housing regression by adding non-iid FEMNIST handwriting classification on Facebook Ego and Florentine Families. Figure 5 also adds a Housing experiment on the Misskey graph. The original privacy-accounting graph coverage is retained.

E2.justification: D-MF, which applies centralized matrix-factorization correlations locally, is removed from Appendix C.1 and the corresponding Housing comparisons. The other comparator memberships in retained experiments remain stable; extending existing baselines to FEMNIST does not introduce new comparison methods.

E3.justification: The added FEMNIST evaluation introduces ten handwriting styles per node, CNN training with cross-entropy, accuracy measurements, and cyclic participation (20,16). These substantially extend the experimental design. The retained Housing experiment still uses its width-64 MLP, mean-square error, and (20,19) participation scheme.

E4.justification: The additional PeerTube convergence analysis at mu=1 in v1 Figure 5b disappears. The Ego learning trajectory largely survives in Figure 3, although its D-MF comparison is lost. v2 Figure 4 adds fixed-budget FEMNIST accuracy trajectories, producing a limited change in convergence diagnostics.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly identifies the FEMNIST Figure 4 error bands as 95% confidence intervals. v1 already reports Housing averages over 20 runs and PNDP minimum, maximum, and mean bars. FEMNIST also uses 20 runs; no increase in the retained experiments' run counts or new seed protocol is stated.

E6.justification: v2 adds FEMNIST accuracy results and Misskey Housing results, while removing D-MF series, the supplementary PeerTube learning curve, and the highest-budget points from the retained Housing appendix plots. Main PNDP findings and the Housing claims of 31% lower test loss and a twofold privacy-budget reduction remain unchanged. These are additions and omissions, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: Appendix A.7 adds a formal workload and update expression for time-varying gossip, and Remark 13 adds time and space complexity bounds. Section 5 corrects the non-uniqueness explanation and the interpretation of B-dagger B as a row-space projection. The central privacy theorem and principal appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged after renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: a unified decentralized MF framework, generalized privacy guarantees, tighter accounting, and superior MAFALDA-SGD performance. The new experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 explains why column-echelon structure accommodates causal observations under partial network visibility and corrects the projection interpretation. Remark 13 makes computational bottlenecks explicit and suggests correlation restarts. The existing explanation linking graph size, local batch size, and privacy remains.

D1.justification: A new Reproducibility section supplies an access location for a reported open-source MFDL implementation. v2 also identifies L-BFGS, documents the FEMNIST CNN configuration, and specifies Jean Zay's V100 partition and Grid'5000 resources. These disclosures do not establish changes to the optimizer or hardware used for retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds Caldas et al. (2018) for LEAF/FEMNIST and Gil et al. (2013) for Renyi divergence. The related-work positioning remains substantially unchanged. The Fedivertex title, year, and venue update refers to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes comprise targeted language and cross-reference corrections, explanatory remarks, new Appendix A.7 and C.2 subsections, and a Reproducibility section, rather than extensive narrative rewriting.

P2.justification: The conference template changes typography, author layout, headers, and document-wide placement. New FEMNIST Figures 4 and 6 are added; the Housing appendix display changes from three horizontal panels to a four-panel grid with revised legends and axis ranges. The old supplementary Figure 5 disappears, and Table 1 is relocated.

improvement.justification: FEMNIST broadens evidence beyond one tabular regression task, while explicit confidence intervals, implementation information, and code-access instructions improve documentation. However, removing D-MF eliminates the closest comparison testing the benefit of decentralized-specific correlation over existing MF approaches; supplementary PeerTube convergence evidence is also lost. Broader evaluation and weaker comparative controls affect different important aspects of quality, leaving the net direction uncertain.
